headline: Price stuck at the mean line with 1.1M BTC of underwater short-term coins at $80–82K overhead; December hike odds near 75%.
summary: Price closed 0.19% below the true market mean; the $76K bucket below holds ~360K BTC bought in October, while ~1.1M BTC of short-term coins sit underwater at $80–82K and may sell on a return to breakeven. STH-SOPR 0.9974 is below 1 for a 3rd day, stablecoins are −1.38% over 7 days and the Coinbase premium is at its low: buyers have not returned. Bull day 24, no exit trigger; this week watch the Nov 3 midterms and Nov 6 payrolls.

overview.lead: Price is back at the lower edge of the true market mean, but overhead sits a large block of new buyers just pushed underwater and the support below comes from people who bought in October; neither flows nor macro give it a reason to push higher.

news.title: Binance reopened withdrawals in phases on Nov 1, bitcoin first, with phase one covering 15 chains; it says company funds now cover ~95% of the $6.3B stolen
news.read: Exchange credit risk eased another notch (90% the day before); the remaining 5% are tokens outside the top ten. Reopening may bring a rush of withdrawals: our exchange supply was −0.79% over 7 days (Oct 31, before the reopening). If it drops sharply in the next two editions, that is mostly users pulling coins, not accumulation, and should not be read as buying. Industry event; does not affect the market stage.

news.title: CME FedWatch puts December quarter-point hike odds near 75%; the Fed held last week with inflation above 2%; October payrolls due Nov 6, consensus +75K, unemployment 4.2%
news.read: Market bets have flipped from cuts to a hike, a headwind for non-yielding BTC. Our 10-year yield is 4.98% and real yield 2.63% (FRED Oct 29); stablecoins −$8.2B over 30 days and the Coinbase premium at its series low fit a tightening dollar backdrop (coincident, not proof of cause). A strong payrolls print could lift hike odds further. Does not affect the cycle call.

news.title: Nasdaq fell 2.0% last week to 25,437, S&P 500 −0.57%; this week brings the Nov 3 US midterms and Apple, AMD and Palantir earnings testing AI spending
news.read: BTC's 30-day correlation with the Nasdaq is 0.66 (FRED Oct 29); if tech keeps falling, BTC is unlikely to rally on its own. The election could change the path of crypto market-structure legislation (the CLARITY Act), a medium-term theme. Short-term event; does not affect the cycle call.

news.title: Total stablecoin supply fell to $298.5B, the lowest since August, down $3.1B since Oct 28; USDT −$5.3B and USDC −$4.0B year to date (unverified)

Stablecoins are crypto's cash, and a steady decline means less buying power on venues, in the same direction as the Coinbase premium sitting at its low. Flows backdrop; does not affect the market stage.

news.title: Strategy posted $20.9B Q3 operating income (mostly unrealized BTC gains), holds 848,517 BTC at an average $75,446, and has sold ~$431.8M of BTC this year to fund preferred dividends and buybacks
news.read: The largest corporate holder's average cost of 75,446 nearly overlaps our STH cost of 75,834 (bitcoin-data Oct 26), making this zone its paper break-even; new preferred issuance has not been confirmed as restarted, so this buyer is not stepping in for now. findings.title: New $76K coins below, underwater $80–82K coins above: price pinned at the mean
findings.lean_why: A large block of new buyers just went underwater overhead and will sell on breakeven, while support below comes from October buyers whose cost sits close to price, and dollar flows are leaving: up is harder than down.
findings.what: Question: with price hugging the true market mean (close 78,239 vs mean 78,391, −0.19%, bitcoin-data Oct 26), how big is the breakeven selling above versus the support below? CheckOnChain (actual coin age, data date Nov 1): short-term holders 3.676M BTC at an average cost of 75,167; thickest buckets $80K 593K, $62K 533K, $82K 511K BTC. Long-term holders 16.428M BTC at a cost of 49,389; the thickest above price are $84K 807K and $90K 389K BTC.
findings.why: Two points in time (modeled, Oct 1 → Oct 31): of the 3.683M BTC short-term holders then, 1.070M BTC moved, most at $84K (291K), $76K (176K) and $82K (164K); the 1.260M BTC bought since and not yet moved is concentrated at $80K (472K), $76K (362K) and $82K (202K). So most underwater coins at $80–82K belong to October newcomers, and the $76K layer is also new buyers whose cost is only ~3% below price. Fact: high-price coins above $88K that price never revisited fell from 3.984M to 3.887M BTC (−96K), so old coins are still trickling out. Behavior check: STH-SOPR 0.9974 (Nov 1) is below 1 for a 3rd day and short-term holders realized 3,058 BTC of losses vs 3,863 BTC of profit (ratio down from 3.54 a week earlier to 1.26), so new buyers are still taking small losses; net realized P/L turned +$152M on Oct 31, so losses are not widening. Contradiction: 9.87% funding shows leveraged longs still betting up, but the Coinbase premium 7-day average of −0.186% (series low) and stablecoins at −1.38% over 7 days show spot buyers have not returned.
findings.alt: Paper losses do not mean selling: newcomers at $80–82K may hold. Per-UTXO data count exchange wallet reshuffles as turnover, and wallet moves around Binance's reopening could inflate October's turnover. The split of changes is modeled: the modeled STH total differs from actual by −1.0% with 9.1% in the wrong bucket, and the modeled cost differs from bitcoin-data by −0.26%; URPD data date Oct 31. The true market mean is bitcoin-data's Oct 26 value (about 6 days late), and the whole series was revised down on Oct 30.
findings.history: Our short/long-term cohort split only exists since 2026-10-27, so there is no comparable history; the price-near-mean signal has run 2 days, and the previous break was Oct 29 (see 2026-10-29-1).
findings.so: Scenarios (conditional, CheckOnChain Nov 1): at a 78,000 close ~1.93M BTC of short-term coins are underwater; at 76,000 that rises to ~2.43M (+490K, mostly the new $76K layer); further down to 66,000 it only reaches 2.55M (thin supply), jumping to 2.97M at 64,000. Logic chain: October's turnover stacked new coins at $76–82K, so there are holders on both sides of this range; dollar flows have not returned, so the buyers needed to absorb 1.1M BTC of breakeven supply above have not appeared; if $76K fails, there is no thick layer below until $66K. The market stage and exit framework are unchanged.
findings.next: By Nov 9: a close above 82,000 means breakeven supply at $80–82K was absorbed, refuting the ceiling; a close below 75,000 means the new $76K layer failed, refuting the floor.
